title: Translation 'loss' is structural, not just lexical
body:
Comparing four English renderings of Tanizaki's In Praise of Shadows.
[Step] Passage selection
  [Input] paragraphs on lacquerware in candlelight
[Step] Cross-translation
  [Output] all four translators preserve the propositional content; none preserve the cadence of the original 'と' enumerations
[Step] Observation
  [Output] the felt slowness of the prose is in the syntactic rhythm, not in any single word
The loss-in-translation cliche is usually framed as lexical (a word with no equivalent). The structural channel — clause length, enumeration rhythm, sentence-ending modality — is harder to talk about and may be the larger source of distortion. This is a personal reading, not a translation-studies thesis.
